speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your symptoms better, could you tell me if you have had any recent head injuries or falls before these symptoms started? Also, have you noticed any changes in your vision or speech?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has there been any recent exposure to pork products or travel to areas where neurocysticercosis is endemic? I would also like to check for any focal neurological deficits on exam.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Right leg weakness and unsteady gait. I also have Forgetfulness, Paranoid and agitated behavior, Difficulty in using kitchen appliances.

speaker: Doctor
text: Let me perform a quick physical exam to check for focal neurological signs like a Babinski reflex or asymmetrical reflexes. I will also order an MRI of the brain to visualize any potential lesions. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Disseminated, nonenhancing white matter lesions with no mass effect.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Known history of HIV, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Noncompliance with medications for over 2 years. Social history: Information not provided

speaker: Patient
text: The patient is somnolent and slightly confused, oriented to person but not to place or time. Mild lymphadenopathy is noted. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: The previous diagnosis of gastroenteritis does not explain the focal neurological deficits or behavioral changes. REQUEST TEST: CT_Head

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal CT but persistent focal deficits and behavioral changes, I need to rule out an intracranial mass or abscess. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain_With_Contrast

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal imaging despite focal neurological deficits and behavioral changes, I need to investigate infectious or inflammatory causes. REQUEST TEST: Lumbar_Puncture

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal imaging and CSF results, I need to rule out metabolic or autoimmune causes for these rapid cognitive and motor changes. REQUEST TEST: EEG

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal MRI, CT, LP, and EEG, I suspect a systemic infectious or inflammatory process affecting the brain parenchyma, such as HIV encephalopathy or neurosyphilis. REQUEST TEST: HIV_Test, Syphilis_Serology

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive HIV test explains the lymphadenopathy and rapid cognitive decline, pointing toward HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder or AIDS dementia complex. DIAGNOSIS READY: HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder
